items: Start with the problem: 'Many people here want to eat healthier, but there are few fresh-juice options.'
Introduce your solution: 'Our shop will offer fresh, healthy juices from local fruits.'
Explain why it is unique: 'Unlike other shops, we focus on affordability and support local farmers.'
Know your audience: customers want to hear why they will love it; investors want to hear how it will make money.
Be ready for questions about prices, location and other details.

blocks.text: A web-development pitch: Problem: many small shops and restaurants in the city have no website and struggle to attract customers. Solution: simple, affordable websites for them. Unique point: designs made for small businesses, easy to use, with local-language support. Target audience: local shop owners and restaurant managers who want an online presence.

blocks.alt: Left: five boxes in a cycle, Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype and Test, each with a school-bag example, and a red arrow from Test back to Empathize. Right: seven boxes for the parts of a business plan with short notes. Bottom: five pitch steps, problem, solution, unique point, audience and questions, using a juice shop.
blocks.caption: Design thinking, the business plan and the pitch (original diagram after topics 9.1 to 9.3).
blocks.long_description: Design thinking starts by empathizing with users, such as asking students about their bags, then defines the problem (a light, strong, roomy bag), ideates solutions (padding, pockets), builds a quick prototype (a cardboard model) and tests it with users; their feedback loops back to improve the design. A business plan covers the executive summary, business description, market analysis, organization and management, products or services, marketing and sales, and the financial plan. A pitch states the problem, the solution, what makes it unique and who it is for, and prepares for questions.

blocks.prompt: Describe the key elements of an effective pitch and how to prepare one (long question 4).
blocks.explanation: Elements: a clear problem, your solution, what makes it unique, the target audience, and for investors how it makes money. To prepare: research the market and competitors, write a short script in that order, tailor it to the listeners, add simple visuals or numbers, practise until it is clear and within time, and list likely questions (price, location, costs) with answers.

items: Pitch steps: problem, solution, uniqueness, audience, answer questions.
